Key observations from the test image:
- Dense population of small, discrete, raised **black dots/specks** scattered across the entire leaf surface
- Leaf tissue transitioning from green (upper) to tan/brown (lower)
- Black structures appear slightly glossy and embossed
- Midrib area shows reddish-brown discoloration
- No pustules, no powdery coating, no discrete lesion shapes — just densely packed black bodies

Top candidates: **Tar_spot** (raised black stromata), **Physoderma_brown_spot** (dark dots on midrib/sheath). Let me check reference images.

Excellent match! The Tar_spot reference (bottom-right panel) shows nearly identical appearance to the test image — brown leaf tissue with densely scattered small raised black stromata, and green tissue remaining in patches. The Physoderma reference shows distinctly different symptomatology (yellow stippling + dark midrib lesions, clustered dots on sheath).

Let me view a few more references to confirm and rule out alternatives.

Both rust diseases show orange-red pustules — clearly different from the jet-black raised dots in the test image.

Let me view two more references to complete my minimum of 6.

Gray leaf spot shows rectangular vein-bounded lesions; Northern corn leaf blight shows large cigar-shaped lesions — both completely different from the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**

- **Test image**: Corn leaf covered in dense, small, discrete **raised black dots** (stromata) scattered across the entire blade; tissue transitions from green to brown/tan; reddish-brown midrib
- **Tar_spot reference**: Virtually identical — the bottom-right panel of the collage shows the exact same pattern: black embossed dots on browning leaf tissue with green patches remaining
- **Ruled out**: Common rust / Southern rust (orange-red pustules), Physoderma brown spot (yellow stippling + dark midrib clusters, different pattern), Gray leaf spot (elongated rectangular lesions), Northern corn leaf blight (large cigar-shaped lesions)

The raised, glossy, jet-black stromata densely covering the leaf surface with the characteristic transition from green to necrotic brown tissue is pathognomonic for Tar spot (*Phyllachora maydis*).
